newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ANI says Ellicott report delayed.
newsitem.headline: ANI says Ellicott report delayed.

text.p: Engineering group Australian National Industries Ltd said on Monday it will have to wait several weeks before a final decision will be made on the report into its acquisition of German environmental business ABT.
"Due to the nature of the additional information requested, it may take several weeks to arrive at a final decision on an appropriate course of action," ANI said in a brief statement.

ANI commissioned Queens Counsel Bob Ellicott last year to look into its controversial purchase of the loss making ABT from media baron Kerry Packer in 1989, when Packer controlled the Sydney-based engineering group.
ANI said the Ellicott report has been received by the board and is under review as to what action should be taken pursuant to the report's analysis.
It said in accordance with Ellicott's recommendations, further information has been requested from lawyers Malleson Stephen Jaques, who assisted Ellicott in conducting his enquiry.
ABT was mainly responsible for the A$233.6 million writedown in ANI's Holter unit in the 1995/96 year due to cost overuns and delays associated with ABT's waste to energy projects.
Packer's family company Consolidated Press Holdings Ltd sold its controlling stake in ANI two weeks after it sold ABT to ANI.
Ellicott, a former Australian Attorney-General and Federal judge, has travelled to Germany to talk to Holter executives and to Consolidated Press.
The report was orginally due late last year, but was delayed due to Ellicott's ill health.
ANI shares closed 1.5 cents lower at A$1.43.
